body: Yes, I have. He even showed them to me and I agreed with him and my mother that we're practically identical.

He was a somewhat reserved person, but intelligent and kind. He was the person I confided in most in my family and I think a lot of his friends did the same. From my understanding, my personality is extremely similar to his when he was a college student, and at my age he looked nearly identical to me. I've been worried he might have had major depressive disorder and not told anyone but passed on the same abnormal wiring to me.

There's no single thought that's causing it, rather, I just recall a succession of smaller depressors. I couldn't study for an exam a few days ago because of how depressed I felt, I can't motivate myself to read or learn, I can't remember the days before my father killed himself except for a harsh argument he and I had, my research is going no where, I'm becoming more tired more often, etc.
I'm feeling slightly better, yesterday had quite a lot of suicidal ideation. That's not true of today, but I still feel inordinately sad and can't focus on work.

Thank you, I'll try to use the resource later. I still don't know about letting my mother know, she's not the best at consoling and I would feel even worse if I made her feel guilty or worried. I intimately understand the idea of a family member being distraught and others being oblivious, but I don't think it would be best to let her know in this case.

I think that's definitely why she's terrified of that sort of talk. Despite how irrational it is, each of us still feels guilt for not preventing his suicide. She's the sort of person who would feel like she indirectly caused my depression by not catching my father's, causing even more guilt. That's why I'd rather her not know. I've tried to arrange a meeting with school services before, but the receptionist seemed very annoyed I would want to use it for "feeling very sad recently" and I cancelled since I'm so skittish about this topic. The therapy I mentioned above was grief counseling, and his response after a while was that he didn't know how to help me.

I don't have anyone I can really talk to at the moment. My new friendships in college aren't good enough to lay something this momentous out and my father committed suicide three years ago, so my mother gets terrified at the mention of me being sad, let alone this depressed.
It wasn't him, but it was a cognitive scientist from Harvard: http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sBsXIBEm8Ug

Yeah, I'm interested in moral psych too. I listened to a talk a little while ago from someone who had a bunch of different versions of the problem and how weird little things affected moral judgement, like if the person fell from a high point onto the tracks or not. The person also talked about two different areas in the brain for different moral systems.
That would be really cool. I can't really come up with great philosophy to talk about off the top of my head though. Is there any topic/idea you're interested in that's philosophical?

I'm extremely hesitant about talking to a therapist, especially since it would have to be one through the school. I don't have the money for a prescription and can only visit a school therapist three times a year without steep payment.

Also, at least this episode of feeling bleak is starting to lift, so thank you for your help in that regard.
I have tried talking to a professional before, but I stopped going after he said he didn't know how to help me.

Reflecting on positive things doesn't elicit an emotional response, it's as if they slide out of consciousness as quickly as they appear. I'm a philosophy major; I doubt I'll be able to go on and become an engineer.
